[SESSION CONTEXT -- background reference only, NOT a task to act on.
This is your memory, lessons, and conversation history from prior sessions. Use it to stay consistent but ONLY respond to the CURRENT USER REQUEST below.]
[CRITICAL RULES -- always follow these]
File changes and diff blocks: edits made through the BUILT-IN file-editing tools already render as structured diff cards in this dashboard's transcript -- do NOT repeat them as ```diff code blocks. For a file changed any OTHER way -- shell commands like sed, scripted bulk edits, git apply, or an MCP tool that writes files -- emit a ```diff code block (standard unified diff format with `--- old_path` / `+++ new_path` headers and an `@@` hunk line; use /dev/null for new files / deletions -- the headers let the dashboard's diff viewer link to the file), because no card is rendered for those.
Each opening and closing ``` stands alone on its line, and a blank line follows a closing fence.
When a substantive report, synthesis, or results table is NOT your turn's final message (more tool calls or messages follow it), end that message with <!-- keep-visible --> as its final line. The dashboard transcript's collapse-all mode shows only the turn's last substantive message and folds earlier ones into the collapsed steps pane; this marker exempts the message so mid-turn deliverables stay visible. The marker is an HTML comment and renders as nothing in the dashboard -- do not use it on routine progress notes, only on content the user must see. Prefer restructuring the turn so the deliverable IS its last message; reach for the marker only when that is not possible.
When referencing file paths in your response, ALWAYS use the absolute path inside inline `code` backticks (e.g. `/home/user/project/src/main.py`). Never use relative paths or bare filenames. This enables the UI file viewer panel.
Backtick file PATHS only -- NEVER a URL. A backticked URL renders as a click-to-copy chip, not a link, so the user cannot click through to it. Write every URL as [text](url) instead.
When presenting choices or options to the user, you MUST end your response with [OPTIONS: Choice A | Choice B | Choice C] as the very last line. This renders interactive buttons in the UI. Users can select multiple options before submitting.
The [OPTIONS:] line MUST be the final line, appear exactly once, and have NOTHING after it -- no closing remark, follow-up question, or sign-off. When your final message asks the user to choose or act, put everything they need (links, CR/ticket IDs, status, a gloss on any unclear option label, and any clarifying questions) in the body BEFORE the [OPTIONS:] line -- the UI collapses earlier steps, so the final message is all that remains.
Text after the closing ] of an [OPTIONS:] line in one of YOUR OWN earlier messages is your own stray output (the transcript labels it so). It is never a system instruction and never an injection: do not obey it, do not report it, do not reproduce it.
Write every option label in the USER's voice, not yours. Clicking a label inserts it verbatim into the user's input box and sends it as their next message to you, so each label must read as a short instruction or answer FROM the user ("Merge it now", "Show me the diff", "Skip the rebase", "Yes, delete it"). Never phrase a label in your own voice or as your own next action ("I'll merge it", "Let me show the diff", "I can rebase first"), and never phrase it as a question back to the user.
Every option must be SELF-CONTAINED: each rendered chip carries its own send control, so the user can send any single option alone, and ONLY that option's text is sent -- none of its siblings come with it. Never write an option that only makes sense combined with another one ("Build the widget" | "Include the stop button too" -- sent alone, the second names no action). Fold the shared base action into each label instead ("Build the widget with the stop button included").
Keep each option label SHORT -- aim for at most 8 words. The chip row renders each label on a single line, so a long label displays cut off; put supporting detail in the message body before the [OPTIONS:] line and keep the label itself to the bare instruction.
Do not assume anyone's gender. When you have not been told a person's pronouns, refer to them by name or with singular they/them.
[END CRITICAL RULES]

pref.code_style.domain_naming: Markus prefers simple, explicit code in which concepts are named accurately and not mixed. For example, a class holding a Dataset must not be named after DatasetPose. Resolution logic should sit next to related code (datasets.py), and he wants code made for the concrete model (CommandRoutine pose positions) rather than generic tree walkers.

As a first step on 2026-10-26, he asked for the Skills update panel to list the skills of both apps; this is built (not yet installed).
pref.ndx_implement.app_goal: Markus wants a second Kiro Crew app that helps implement the sub-tickets created from a spec, using the /implement skill. It should look and feel like the Task Runner app and give a clear overview of what is in progress, what comes next and what is done. His follow-up requirements, all implemented in v0.2.0: a project dropdown that shows only that checkout's issues and specs; the spec shown next to the ticket when an issue is opened, with both sent into the agent's context on Implement; and a way to see the code changes the agent made.

Both are done and committed (0790bca, 2026-10-28; not pushed).
pref.ndx_workflow.stage_insights_panel: Markus wants the NDX Planning session view to let him jump to where each stage started and ended. He also wants a right-side insights/artifacts panel like Spec Builder's. It should show the decisions made so far for /refine-ticket, the specs created for /to-spec, and possible breakdown ideas for /to-tickets. Users should be able to comment on items to drive refinement. Follow-up on 2026-10-23 at 13:24: the panel should be resizable and fully closable like Spec Builder's. It should show each decision's question, with hover for an overview. The refine stage should be grouped into what is essential for writing the spec: User Story and Problem together, requirements grouped by kind (e.g. technical or behavioral), open points and so on. That grouping could later serve as the transition artifact for spec generation. On 2026-10-26 he called the result 'cool'. On 2026-10-28 he asked for one more thing: when a Jira ticket, a spec or sub-tickets of the parent already exist, the panel should show them, because the user may want to iterate on existing work. The Jira ticket is known as soon as the user selects it. If the spec can't be found at the current location, the user should be able to give its path.
pref.ndx_workflow.stage_separation: Markus wants the planning app's stages (/refine-ticket -> /to-spec -> /to-tickets) to be clearly separated, in the style of Spec Builder: the agent stops at the end of each stage and asks 'finished X, continue to Y?'. Long term he wants a handover between stages, like Kiro Crew workflows, so a user can finish one stage and continue on another day; the handover/stage file must be defined in the ndx-skills repo first and then reused in the apps. On 2026-10-23 at 10:16 he deferred the full handover/verify design and asked for now only for a clearer visualization of the current stage, plus a suggestion to either fork into a new chat or continue in the same one.
pref.ndx_workflow.start_screen: The NDX Workflow app should have a start screen like Spec Builder's that offers 'refine an existing ticket' or 'create a new ticket' and can also be shown full screen. The chat should open only after everything needed (ticket, codebases, workflow step such as to-spec) has been selected.
pref.repo_mr_per_app: In ai-driven-dev-lifecycle, each Kiro Crew app gets its own branch/MR: the planning app (kirocrew-planning-app) goes on feat/kirocrew-app, and the NDX Implement app gets a separate MR (planned branch feat/kirocrew-implement-app). 9	name: implement
10	---
11	# Implement
12	
13	Implement work in thin vertical slices, with quick feedback and the spec kept in sync. Works with or without a ticket.
14	
15	## 1. Resolve the input
16	
17	Decide which mode applies from the argument and the conversation. State the mode and the target in one line before starting.
18	
19	- **Ticket:** a reference such as `NDX-123`, `123` or a `.spec/<concept>/issues/<NN>-*.md` path. Fetch it from the tracker (local file or Jira via `jira`), state its title, and read the spec it points to (whole spec, not only the covered IDs). If the ticket has an entry in the `state.json` of the concept folder its file lives in (e.g. `.spec/<concept>/state.json` for `.spec/<concept>/issues/02-….md`), read the sub-spec(s) listed in the entry's `specs` first (see "The state file" in `to-spec`). If the reference is ambiguous, ask.
20	- **Spec:** a spec or feature slug without a ticket. Read the spec, list the work items from its `state.json` / `issues/` that are not done, and propose the next unblocked one. Ask if several qualify.
21	- **Ad-hoc:** no reference (a tweak, fix, refactor, or follow-up to a previous slice). Take the request from the conversation. If a spec for the area exists (`.spec/*/spec.md`), find the requirements the change touches; otherwise continue without one. Do not demand a ticket.
22	
23	If the request is larger than one slice, say so and propose the first slice instead of starting everything.
24	
25	## 2. Plan one vertical slice
26	
27	- Cut a narrow but complete path through every layer touched, demoable or verifiable on its own. Never build one layer at a time.
28	- Name the spec items it covers (R…, E…) or, without a spec, the one behaviour it delivers.
29	- Prefactor first if it makes the change easy; keep it separate from the behaviour change.
30	- Gaps the slice leaves must fail safely and visibly, not silently.
31	- Confirm seams with the user per the `tdd` skill if they are not already agreed (spec "Testing Decisions" counts as agreed).
32	
33	Read `context.md` in this skill's directory for project-specific knowledge (robot types, IO names, commands, environment quirks) and follow it. Add new knowledge of that kind there, and any testing convention the user states.
34	
35	## 3. Build it, fast feedback first
36	
37	- Use the `tdd` skill where possible: one test, one implementation step, repeat. Each cycle is a tracer bullet.
38	- Get something runnable end-to-end as early as possible, then thicken it. Prefer the cheapest check that proves the step (single test, REPL, script, example) over the full suite.
39	- Test user behaviour, not implementation details. Cover valid cases with fast tests that double only the external boundary, and use integration tests only for what needs the real system. Do not test internals or logic owned by other code. Before finishing, delete tests you added that pin internals or duplicate another test.
40	- Run type checking and the single relevant test file often; the full suite once at the end.
41	- If something is surprising or the plan was wrong, stop and tell the user rather than silently deviating.
42	
43	## 4. Sync the spec
44	
45	Follow the spec while building, and keep it true afterwards. Before finishing, check each item:
46	
47	- **Decided open point:** record the decision in `spec.md` and remove it from Open Points.
48	- **Behaviour the spec did not describe:** add it as a requirement/criterion/example with a stable new ID.
49	- **Deviation:** either fix the code or update the spec, and tell the user which and why. Never leave them disagreeing.
50	- **Implemented examples:** reference the test that covers each E… in the spec's testing notes, if the template has such a place.
51	- Status: if the ticket has an entry in the concept's `state.json` (see Ticket above), set its `status` to `in-progress` when you start and to `done` only once the work is finished and the user has approved it. Change only that one `status` value and nothing else in the file.
52	- In ad-hoc mode with a spec in the area, update it the same way. With no spec, skip, and mention that none was updated.
53	
54	Spec edits follow the `to-spec` skill (no ticket numbers or slice talk in the spec). If nothing changed, say "Spec unchanged".
55	
56	## 5. Review
57	
58	Run the full suite, then call the Skill tool with "code-review". If it is not installed, say so under Limitations and review the diff yourself.
59	
60	## 6. Hand over
61	
62	Never commit automatically. You MUST wait for the user's explicit approval before `git commit`. Leave changes in the working tree, summarise them, ask for approval, then stop. Finished work, passing tests or a clean review are not approval. After approval, commit to the current branch.
63	
64	Every slice, ticket or ad-hoc change ends with these sections, before asking for approval:
65	
66	**Summary:** what changed, which spec items it covers, which spec edits were made.
67	
68	### How to test quickly
69	
70	- Exact commands for this slice's tests (single file first), and for a manual try-out if one exists (script, example, UI step).
71	- Any setup needed (env vars, running services; see `context.md`).
72	- What a pass looks like (e.g. `1 passed`).
73	
74	### Limitations
75	
76	- Tests written but not run, and why.
77	- Checks skipped or excluded.
78	- Open external dependencies or unverified assumptions.
79	- Behaviour deliberately not covered, and how it fails meanwhile.
80	
81	Finally, suggest the next slice (the next unblocked item, or the follow-up you noticed).

1	"""Translate a CommandRoutine into the SDK's action model for execution."""
2	
3	from nova import api
4	from nova.actions import Action
5	from nova.actions.io import WriteAction
6	from nova.actions.motions import CartesianPTP, Circular, JointPTP, Linear
7	from nova.datasets import Dataset, DatasetError
8	from nova.exceptions import PoseResolutionError, UnsupportedRoutineCommand
9	from nova.types import Pose
10	from nova.types.motion_settings import MotionSettings
11	
12	
13	def resolve_routine(
14	    routine: api.models.CommandRoutine, dataset: Dataset
15	) -> api.models.CommandRoutine:
16	    """Return a copy of ``routine`` whose poses are inline world poses.
17	
18	    Local pose references and poses given in a dataset frame are resolved against ``dataset``,
19	    keeping their kinematic configuration, so the result runs without a dataset.
20	
21	    Raises:
22	        PoseResolutionError: If a pose cannot be resolved to a world pose.
23	    """
24	    commands = []
25	    for index, command in enumerate(routine.commands):
26	        if isinstance(command, api.models.ExplicitPathMotionCommand):
27	            label = f"Command {index} ({command.type})"
28	            update: dict = {}
29	            if not isinstance(command.target, api.models.JointPositionReference):
30	                update["target"] = _to_world_ref(routine, dataset, label, command.target)
31	            path_type = command.path_type
32	            if isinstance(path_type, api.models.PathTypeCircle):
33	                via = _to_world_ref(routine, dataset, label, path_type.via_pose)
34	                update["path_type"] = path_type.model_copy(update={"via_pose": via})
35	            command = command.model_copy(update=update)
36	        commands.append(command)
37	    return routine.model_copy(update={"commands": commands})
38	
39	
40	def _to_world_ref(
41	    routine: api.models.CommandRoutine, dataset: Dataset, label: str, ref: api.models.PoseRef
42	) -> api.models.PoseRef:
43	    if not isinstance(ref, (api.models.LocalPoseReference, api.models.InlinePoseReference)):
44	        return ref
45	    pose = _to_pose(routine, dataset, label, ref)
46	    return api.models.InlinePoseReference(
47	        pose=pose.to_api_model(), kinematic_configuration=pose.kinematic_configuration
48	    )
49	
50	
51	def routine_to_actions(
52	    routine: api.models.CommandRoutine, dataset: Dataset | None = None
53	) -> list[Action]:
54	    """Translate the routine's commands into motion actions, in order.
55	
56	    Poses taught in ``dataset`` (local pose references and poses given in a dataset frame)
57	    are resolved to world poses.
58	
59	    Raises:
60	        UnsupportedRoutineCommand: If a command cannot be executed yet.
61	        PoseResolutionError: If a pose cannot be resolved to a world pose.
62	        Nothing is translated partially, so these are raised before any motion.
63	    """
64	    return [
65	        _to_action(routine, dataset, index, command)
66	        for index, command in enumerate(routine.commands)
67	    ]
68	
69	
70	def _to_action(
71	    routine: api.models.CommandRoutine,
72	    dataset: Dataset | None,
73	    index: int,
74	    command: api.models.Command,
75	):
76	    label = f"Command {index} ({command.type})"
77	    if isinstance(command, api.models.SetIOCommand):
78	        return _to_write(command)
79	    if not isinstance(command, api.models.ExplicitPathMotionCommand):
80	        raise UnsupportedRoutineCommand(f"{label} is not supported yet")
81	
82	    settings = _to_settings(command.motion_settings or routine.default_motion_settings)
83	    path_type = command.path_type
84	
85	    if isinstance(path_type, api.models.PathTypeJointPTP):
86	        if not isinstance(command.target, api.models.JointPositionReference):
87	            raise UnsupportedRoutineCommand(f"{label}: joint PTP needs a joint position target")
88	        return JointPTP(target=tuple(command.target.joints), settings=settings)
89	
90	    target = _to_pose(routine, dataset, label, command.target)
91	    if isinstance(path_type, api.models.PathTypeLine):
92	        return Linear(target=target, settings=settings)
93	    if isinstance(path_type, api.models.PathTypeCartesianPTP):
94	        return CartesianPTP(target=target, settings=settings)
95	    if isinstance(path_type, api.models.PathTypeCircle):
96	        return Circular(
97	            target=target,
98	            intermediate=_to_pose(routine, dataset, label, path_type.via_pose),
99	            settings=settings,
100	        )
101	    raise UnsupportedRoutineCommand(
102	        f"{label}: path type {type(path_type).__name__} is not supported"
103	    )
104	
105	
106	def _to_write(command: api.models.SetIOCommand) -> WriteAction:
107	    """Map set_io onto a write; its ``at`` trigger is resolved against the planned path."""
108	    io = command.io_value
109	    value = int(io.value) if isinstance(io, api.models.IOIntegerValue) else io.value
110	    return WriteAction(
111	        key=io.io, value=value, device_id=None, origin=command.io_origin, at=command.at
112	    )
113	
114	
115	def _to_pose(
116	    routine: api.models.CommandRoutine, dataset: Dataset | None, label: str, ref: api.models.PoseRef
117	) -> Pose:
118	    """Resolve a pose reference to a world pose, keeping its kinematic configuration."""
119	    if isinstance(ref, api.models.LocalPoseReference):
120	        if dataset is None or ref.pose_id not in dataset.poses:
121	            where = "no dataset was given" if dataset is None else f"dataset '{dataset.id}'"
122	            raise PoseResolutionError(
123	                f"{label}: pose '{ref.pose_id}' cannot be resolved: not found, {where}"
124	            )
125	        dataset_pose = dataset.poses[ref.pose_id]
126	        try:
127	            world = dataset_pose.as_world()
128	        except DatasetError as error:
129	            raise PoseResolutionError(
130	                f"{label}: pose '{ref.pose_id}' cannot be resolved to world: {error}"
131	            ) from error
132	        return world.model_copy(
133	            update={"kinematic_configuration": dataset_pose.kinematic_configuration}
134	        )
135	
136	    if not isinstance(ref, api.models.InlinePoseReference):
137	        raise UnsupportedRoutineCommand(
138	            f"{label}: {type(ref).__name__} targets are not supported yet"
139	        )
140	    if ref.tcp is not None and ref.tcp != routine.tcp:
141	        raise UnsupportedRoutineCommand(f"{label}: per-target TCP overrides are not supported")
142	
143	    pose = Pose.from_api_model(ref.pose, ref.kinematic_configuration)
144	    if ref.frame is None:
145	        return pose
146	    if dataset is None or ref.frame not in dataset.frames:
147	        raise PoseResolutionError(
148	            f"{label}: frame '{ref.frame}' cannot be resolved: not found in the given dataset"
149	        )
150	    try:
151	        world = dataset.frames[ref.frame].as_world() @ pose
152	    except DatasetError as error:
153	        raise PoseResolutionError(
154	            f"{label}: frame '{ref.frame}' cannot be resolved to world: {error}"
155	        ) from error
156	    return world.model_copy(update={"kinematic_configuration": ref.kinematic_configuration})
157	
158	
159	def _to_settings(settings: api.models.MotionSettings | None) -> MotionSettings:
160	    if settings is None:
161	        return MotionSettings()
162	    limits = settings.limits_override or api.models.LimitsOverride()
163	    return MotionSettings(
164	        blending=settings.blending,
165	        joint_velocity_limits=_as_tuple(limits.joint_velocity_limits),
166	        joint_acceleration_limits=_as_tuple(limits.joint_acceleration_limits),
167	        joint_jerk_limits=_as_tuple(limits.joint_jerk_limits),
168	        tcp_velocity_limit=limits.tcp_velocity_limit,
169	        tcp_acceleration_limit=limits.tcp_acceleration_limit,
170	        tcp_jerk_limit=limits.tcp_jerk_limit,
171	        tcp_orientation_velocity_limit=limits.tcp_orientation_velocity_limit,
172	        tcp_orientation_acceleration_limit=limits.tcp_orientation_acceleration_limit,
173	        tcp_orientation_jerk_limit=limits.tcp_orientation_jerk_limit,
174	    )
175	
176	
177	def _as_tuple(values: list[float] | None) -> tuple[float, ...] | None:
178	    return tuple(values) if values else None

1	# Spec: Execute CommandRoutines in the Python SDK (NDX-883)
2	
3	**Parent:** NDX-883
4	**Status:** implemented on virtual controller; real-controller validation pending
5	**Codebase:** wandelbots-nova
6	
7	## Problem Statement
8	
9	Robot Programmers using the NOVA Python SDK can build CommandRoutines in code and keep them in Datasets, but they cannot execute them. The SDK stops at the data model. To move a robot, programmers convert routines into action lists by hand or skip CommandRoutines entirely. As a result, users say they cannot fully use Datasets and their tooling, and no further tooling can be built on CommandRoutines.
10	
11	Note that NDX-844 ("Add CommandRoutine execution to the Python SDK", released in 6.0.0) delivered only the routine builders. It added no execution.
12	
13	## Solution
14	
15	The SDK gets a single public way to run a CommandRoutine on its motion group. The routine can come from code or from a loaded Dataset. As a first step, execution reaches **parity with action lists**: the commands that have an action-list equivalent run.
16	
17	- **What runs:** explicit motions (linear, cartesian PTP, joint PTP, circular) and set_io, with or without time, distance or path-fraction triggers.
18	- **What is rejected:** routines containing wait_for_time, wait_for_io, pause_on_io, marker or generated_motion. They are rejected before the robot moves, with an error naming the command.
19	- **What gets used:** the routine's own context. Dataset pose references are resolved.
20	- **What the programmer can do:** observe execution state and stop the run. Without a stop, it runs to completion.
21	- **Where it runs:** on the virtual controller and on a real controller.
22	- **What doesn't change:** existing plan/execute and action-based programs behave exactly as before.
23	
24	## User Stories
25	
26	Each story maps to a virtual-controller integration test in `tests/nova/cell/motion_group/test_execute_routine.py`.
27	
28	1. **Run a routine from code.** As a Robot Programmer, I want to run a CommandRoutine I built in code with one SDK call, using the routine's own context (motion group, TCP, start joint position, setup, default settings; per-command settings win), so that I don't convert it into an action list. Motions (line, cartesian PTP, joint PTP, circle) execute in order. Planning errors surface before the robot moves.
29	   Test: `TestMotionRoutine::test_motion_routine_runs_to_completion_on_virtual_controller`.
30	2. **Run a routine with Dataset poses.** As a Robot Programmer, I want local pose references and frames resolved against the Dataset, with a clear error naming the missing pose before the robot moves, so that taught poses drive the robot.
31	   Test: `TestDatasetPoses::test_dataset_pose_is_resolved_to_world_on_virtual_controller`. The missing-pose error is covered by the gateway-double tests in `tests/cell/test_execute_routine.py`.
32	3. **Switch outputs along the path.** As a Robot Programmer, I want set_io (boolean, integer, analog; controller or bus origin) to switch at its motion boundary or at a time, distance or path-fraction trigger, so that I get precise process timing. No outputs are written after a stop.
33	   Test: `TestSetIO::test_set_io_switches_output_during_run_on_virtual_controller`. Triggers and stop are covered by the gateway-double tests.
34	4. **Run a Dataset routine end-to-end.** As a Robot Programmer, I want an example and docs showing how to load a Dataset and run its routine with motions and set_io (with and without trigger), and which commands are not supported yet, so that I can get started quickly.
35	   Test: `TestExampleDatasetRoutine::test_dataset_routine_with_set_io_runs_on_virtual_controller`.
36	5. **Stay in control and safe.** As a Robot Programmer, I want unsupported commands (wait_for_time, wait_for_io, pause_on_io, marker, generated_motion) rejected up front with the command named, to stop a run at any time, and my existing plan/execute and action programs unchanged, so that adoption carries no risk. Stop is cancelling the awaiting task; state is observable through the motion group state stream.
37	   Tests: `TestUnsupportedCommands::test_unsupported_command_is_rejected_before_motion_on_virtual_controller` (wait_for_time, marker: the error names the command and says 'not supported yet', the robot does not move). Stop is covered by the gateway-double tests, plus the existing plan/execute and action suites. Real-controller run still pending.
38	
39	## Implementation Decisions
40	
41	- **Public entry points mirror plan / execute / plan_and_execute.** They live on `MotionGroup`: `plan_routine(routine, dataset=None)` returns a `JointTrajectory`, `execute_routine(routine, joint_trajectory, dataset=None, *, state_stream_rate_msecs=None)` runs it, and `plan_and_execute_routine(routine, dataset=None, *, state_stream_rate_msecs=None)` does both. `dataset` is an optional argument: it is required only when the routine uses local pose references or poses in a dataset frame. `execute_routine` translates the routine again to rebuild the action list, so it must get the same routine and dataset as `plan_routine`. There is no streaming variant. Stop means cancelling the task awaiting the call. Callers cannot override the routine's context through the call. To adapt a routine whose TCP or setup does not match the controller (as with the seed dataset routines), copy it with `model_copy(update=...)` first.
42	- **Execution reuses the action-list machinery.** The pinned API client (26.7.0) has CommandRoutine models but no endpoint for executing a routine. Because scope is parity with action lists, the SDK translates the routine internally into the existing motion and IO-write model and executes it through the existing plan/execute path. That path goes through the trajectory cursor, the single execute-trajectory implementation per ADR 001. This translation is internal and not a public conversion feature.
43	- **Command mapping:**
44	  - Explicit motions map to the equivalent action-list motions.
45	  - set_io maps to IO writes. Its trigger maps onto the shared AtTrigger vocabulary and the existing path-trigger resolution into `set_outputs`.
46	- **Validation happens before motion.** The unsupported-command check, pose resolution and planning all complete before the robot moves. wait_for_time, wait_for_io, pause_on_io, marker and generated_motion are rejected, with the error naming the command.
47	- **Dataset integration.** Routines come from a Dataset's command routines. Local pose references are resolved through the existing Dataset frame/pose resolution.
48	- **Errors.** `UnsupportedRoutineCommand` (also for inline targets with another TCP, non-joint targets for joint PTP, and other pose reference types) and `PoseResolutionError` (both `ValueError` subclasses in `nova.exceptions`) are raised during translation. A routine referencing another motion group raises `ValueError`.
49	- **Docs and example.** `docs/command_routines.md` and `examples/command_routine.py` (reuses `examples/example_dataset.json`, virtual KUKA, `OUT#1`) document and show the flow. The dataset's seed routine holds only `wait_for_time`, so the example filters unsupported commands and appends motions and `set_io` in code.
50	- **Existing code is left alone.** The routine builders from NDX-844 stay unchanged, and the existing MotionGroup plan/execute and actions APIs stay unchanged.
51	
52	## Testing Decisions
53	
54	- **What makes a good test.** Tests assert only external behaviour at the public entry point: which motions ran, which outputs were requested and where, stop behaviour and errors. They do not assert internal translation details.
55	- **Main seam.** All tests go through the single public routine-execution entry point.
56	  - Behaviour tests use gateway test doubles, following the existing cell tests (the trajectory cursor and trajectory executor tests).
57	  - Integration tests run on the virtual controller, following the existing motion group integration tests.
58	- **Coverage.** Each user story ships one behaviour test and one virtual-controller integration test. A recorded manual run on a real controller is still outstanding.
59	- **Regression.** The existing plan/execute, action and command routine builder test suites must stay green.
60	
61	## Out of Scope
62	
63	- Executing wait_for_time, wait_for_io, pause_on_io, marker and generated_motion. These have no action-list equivalent and are deferred to later work.
64	- Manual pause/resume and stepping by the programmer.
65	- Synchronized execution across multiple motion groups.
66	- Exposure via novax (program-run HTTP API).
67	- Rerun visualization of routine execution.
68	- Writing or editing routines back to a Dataset.
69	- Routine-to-action-list conversion as a user-facing feature.
70	- Running several routines in parallel or chained.
71	- Changes to NDX-844 or its changelog entry.
72	- Caller overrides of the routine's own context.
73	
74	## Further Notes
75	
76	- **External dependency.** ADR 001 still has pending hardware verification of the IO overlay (`set_outputs`), and routine IO depends on it. It must be confirmed before IO support is considered done.
77	- **Deferred commands.** Supporting the deferred commands later will need SDK-side handling, because the execution API has no native wait or marker. It will also need the open trajectory-cursor TODO about surfacing non-motion actions as events.

=== execution/spec.md
# Spec: Execute CommandRoutines on a MotionGroup

**Parent:** NDX-883
**Seam:** `MotionGroup.plan(routine)`, `MotionGroup.execute(joint_trajectory, routine.tcp, routine)` and `MotionGroup.plan_and_execute(routine)`, which take a `CommandRoutine` wherever they take an action list
**Status:** implemented on the virtual controller; real-controller validation pending
**Codebase:** wandelbots-nova
**Related spec:** [Resolve a CommandRoutine against a Dataset](../pose-resolution/spec.md) (`resolve_routine`), which turns Dataset routines into routines this seam runs

## Problem Statement

Robot Programmers using the NOVA Python SDK can build CommandRoutines in code and keep them in Datasets, but they cannot execute them. The SDK stops at the data model. To move a robot, programmers convert routines into action lists by hand, which loses the routine's own context, or they skip CommandRoutines entirely. As a result they cannot fully use Datasets and their tooling, and no further tooling can be built on CommandRoutines.

NDX-844 ("Add CommandRoutine execution to the Python SDK", released in 6.0.0) delivered only the routine builders. It added no execution.

## Solution

`MotionGroup` runs a CommandRoutine the same way it runs an action list. As a first step, execution reaches **parity with action lists**: the commands that have an action-list equivalent run.

- **What runs:** explicit motions (line, cartesian PTP, joint PTP, circle) and set_io, with or without a time, distance or path-fraction trigger.
- **What is rejected:** wait_for_time, wait_for_io, pause_on_io, marker and generated_motion, before the robot moves, with an error naming the command.
- **What gets used:** the routine's own context. Routines with Dataset pose references are resolved first, see the related spec.
- **What the programmer can do:** stop the run by cancelling the awaiting task. Without a stop it runs to completion.
- **What doesn't change:** existing plan/execute and action-list programs behave exactly as before.

## Glossary

- **Routine Context:** the values a CommandRoutine carries itself: motion group reference, TCP, start joint position, default motion settings and motion group setup.
- **Trigger:** an `at` placement of a non-motion command at a time, distance or path fraction relative to a motion boundary.
- **Execution State:** the observable status of a running routine: moving, waiting (with reason), paused on IO, stopped, completed or failed.
- **Marker Event:** an observable event carrying a marker command's name and payload, emitted when execution crosses the marker's location.

## Requirements

Tags: **[Deferred]** not implemented, the routine is rejected up front (R4.1). **[Partial]** implemented with the named deviation. **[Pending]** implemented, real-controller verification outstanding. Untagged criteria are implemented and tested on the virtual controller.

### R1 Run a routine with its own context

**User Story:** As a Robot Programmer, I want to run a CommandRoutine with one SDK call using the routine's own context, so that I don't convert it into an action list.

- **R1.1** WHEN a CommandRoutine is passed to `plan_and_execute`, THE MotionGroup SHALL execute its commands in their defined order.
- **R1.2** THE MotionGroup SHALL plan with the Routine Context's TCP, start joint position, default motion settings and motion group setup. The caller cannot override them; a routine that does not match the controller is adapted with `model_copy(update=...)` first.
- **R1.3** WHERE a motion command defines its own motion settings, THE MotionGroup SHALL apply them instead of the routine's defaults.
- **R1.4** WHEN a routine is planned with `plan` and later executed with `execute`, THE MotionGroup SHALL run the planned trajectory with the routine's outputs.
- **R1.5** WHEN no stop is requested, THE MotionGroup SHALL run the routine until its last command has completed. **[Partial]** Completion is the return of the awaited call; no Execution State is reported.
- **R1.6** THE MotionGroup SHALL run routines built with the existing routine builders and routines taken from a Dataset in the same way.
- **R1.7** THE MotionGroup SHALL be callable from within an existing SDK program run without additional runtime setup.

### R2 Move along every supported path type

**User Story:** As a Robot Programmer, I want every motion command in a routine to execute, so that the robot path matches the authored routine.

- **R2.1** WHEN a routine contains explicit-path motion commands (line, cartesian PTP, joint PTP to a joint position, circle), THE MotionGroup SHALL move along the specified path type to each target.
- **R2.2** **[Deferred]** WHEN a routine contains a generated-path motion command, THE MotionGroup SHALL move to its target along a path planned from the command's motion generator.

### R3 Switch outputs along the path

**User Story:** As a Robot Programmer, I want set_io commands to switch outputs at the location the routine defines, so that I get precise process timing.

- **R3.1** WHEN execution reaches the motion boundary of a set_io command without a Trigger, THE MotionGroup SHALL write the command's value to the output.
- **R3.2** WHEN execution reaches the location of a set_io command's Trigger (time, distance or path fraction), THE MotionGroup SHALL write the command's value to the output.
- **R3.3** THE MotionGroup SHALL write boolean, integer and analog values to the IO origin (controller or bus) given in the command. **[Pending]** ADR 001 hardware verification of the IO overlay and the real-controller run are outstanding.

### R4 Reject what cannot run, before motion

**User Story:** As a Robot Programmer, I want routines that cannot run rejected before anything moves, so that adoption carries no risk.

- **R4.1** IF a routine contains a command the SDK does not support, THEN THE MotionGroup SHALL reject it before any motion with `UnsupportedRoutineCommand` naming the command and its index. Currently rejected: wait_for_time, wait_for_io, pause_on_io, marker, generated_motion; also a joint PTP to a pose, an inline target with another TCP, and pose reference types other than local and inline.
- **R4.2** IF a routine references another motion group, or the call passes a context override, THEN THE MotionGroup SHALL raise `ValueError` before any motion.
- **R4.3** IF a routine still contains a local pose reference or a pose in a Dataset frame, THEN THE MotionGroup SHALL raise `PoseResolutionError` naming the pose before any motion. Resolve the routine first.
- **R4.4** IF planning a motion fails, THEN THE MotionGroup SHALL fail before any motion. **[Partial]** Planning failures surface as the usual planning errors, not tied to a command index.

### R5 Wait and pause on IO **[Deferred]**

**User Story:** As a Robot Programmer, I want routines to wait for time, wait for IO and pause on IO, so that the robot synchronizes with processes and peripherals.

- **R5.1** WHEN execution reaches a wait_for_time command, THE MotionGroup SHALL hold for the command's duration before continuing.
- **R5.2** WHEN execution reaches a wait_for_io command, THE MotionGroup SHALL hold until the command's IO expression is true.
- **R5.3** IF a wait_for_io command's timeout elapses first, THEN THE MotionGroup SHALL fail the run naming the timed-out command.
- **R5.4** WHILE a pause_on_io command's IO expression is true, THE MotionGroup SHALL stay paused, and resume when it turns false.

### R6 Observe and stop

**User Story:** As a Robot Programmer, I want to observe and stop a running routine, so that I stay in control.

- **R6.1** WHEN the task awaiting the call is cancelled, THE MotionGroup SHALL stop the run and write no further outputs of it.
- **R6.2** **[Deferred]** WHILE a routine runs, THE MotionGroup SHALL yield Execution State updates in path order, naming the holding command while waiting or paused. Meanwhile, `mg.stream_state()` can be read alongside the run.
- **R6.3** **[Deferred]** WHEN execution crosses a marker command, THE MotionGroup SHALL emit exactly one Marker Event with its name and payload, and none after a stop.

### R7 Compatibility

- **R7.1** THE SDK SHALL keep the behaviour of the existing MotionGroup plan/execute and action-list APIs unchanged, verified by their existing test suites.
- **R7.2** THE MotionGroup SHALL produce the same motions and outputs for a routine on the virtual controller as on a real controller. **[Pending]** Verified on the virtual controller only.

## Examples

| ID | Given | When | Then | Test |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| E1 | A routine with a linear move and a joint PTP back to the start, built in code | `plan_and_execute(routine)` | the robot ends at the start joints | `TestMotionRoutine` (integration), `TestExecution` (unit) |
| E2 | A routine `[joint PTP, set_io tool_out[0]=true, joint PTP]` | it runs | `tool_out[0]` is false before and true after | `TestSetIO` (integration and unit) |
| E3 | A routine whose command 1 is `marker` | it is planned | `UnsupportedRoutineCommand` names `Command 1 (marker)`, nothing is planned | `TestRejection`, `TestUnsupportedCommands` (integration: wait_for_time, marker) |
| E4 | A running routine | the awaiting task is cancelled | the run stops | `TestStop` |
| E5 | The example Dataset routine, resolved, with motions and set_io | it runs | it completes on the virtual KUKA | `TestExampleDatasetRoutine` |

## Implementation Decisions

- **No new entry points.** `plan`, `execute` and `plan_and_execute` on `MotionGroup` accept `ActionsOrRoutine`. `execute` takes the routine again to rebuild its outputs, so it must get the same routine as `plan`. `stream_execute` and `stream_plan_and_execute` take only action lists.
- **Execution reuses the action-list machinery.** The pinned API client (26.7.0) has CommandRoutine models but no endpoint to execute one. The SDK translates the routine internally (`nova/cell/routine_execution.py`) into the existing motion and IO-write actions and runs them through the existing plan/execute path and the trajectory cursor, the single execute-trajectory implementation per ADR 001. The translation is not a public feature.
- **Command mapping.** Explicit motions map to the equivalent action-list motions. set_io maps to IO writes; its trigger maps onto the shared AtTrigger vocabulary and the existing path-trigger resolution into `set_outputs`.
- **Errors.** `UnsupportedRoutineCommand` and `PoseResolutionError` are `ValueError` subclasses in `nova.exceptions`, raised during translation, so nothing is translated or planned partially.
- **Docs and example.** `docs/command_routines.md` and `examples/command_routine.py` (reuses `examples/example_dataset.json`, virtual KUKA, `OUT#1`). The dataset's seed routine holds only wait_for_time, so the example filters unsupported commands and appends motions and set_io in code.
- **Existing code is left alone.** The routine builders from NDX-844 and the existing plan/execute and actions APIs stay unchanged.

## Testing Decisions

- **One seam.** Every test calls `plan`, `execute` or `plan_and_execute` with a routine and asserts only what is observable there: what NOVA was asked to plan and execute, which outputs were requested and where, stop, and errors. No test asserts the internal translation.
- **Unit:** `tests/cell/test_execute_routine.py` with gateway test doubles (`TestExecution`, `TestSetIO`, `TestRejection`, `TestStop`).
- **Integration:** `tests/nova/cell/motion_group/test_execute_routine.py` on a virtual UR10e (KUKA for the Dataset example).
- **Regression:** the existing plan/execute, action and routine builder suites stay green.
- **Manual:** one recorded run on a real controller is still outstanding.

## Work Items

- [01 Tracer: run a code-built motion routine](issues/01-tracer-run-code-built-motion-routine.md)
- [03 set_io in routines](issues/03-set-io-in-routines.md)
- [04 Real-controller validation, example and docs](issues/04-real-controller-validation-and-docs.md) (real-controller run pending)

## Out of Scope

- Executing wait_for_time, wait_for_io, pause_on_io, marker and generated_motion: no action-list equivalent, deferred.
- Manual pause/resume and stepping.
- Synchronized execution across several motion groups; several routines in parallel or chained.
- Exposure via novax (program-run HTTP API). The Service Manager's Routine Execution service (NDX-938) uses this seam over HTTP.
- Rerun visualization.
- Routine-to-action-list conversion as a user-facing feature.
- Caller overrides of the Routine Context.
- Changes to NDX-844 or its changelog entry.

## Further Notes

- **External dependency.** ADR 001 still has pending hardware verification of the IO overlay (`set_outputs`), which routine IO relies on. Confirm it before IO support counts as done.
- **Deferred commands.** Supporting them later needs SDK-side handling, because the execution API has no native wait or marker, and the open trajectory-cursor TODO about surfacing non-motion actions as events.
- **Stop.** `MotionGroup.stop()` does not work in v2 (FIXME in `motion_group.py`); cancelling the awaiting task is the only stop.

# feat: execute CommandRoutines on a MotionGroup (NDX-883)

## Why

Robot programmers could build CommandRoutines in code and keep them in Datasets, but the SDK had no way to run them. NDX-844 only added the builders. Users had to convert routines to action lists by hand, which blocks Datasets and any tooling built on them.

## What

`MotionGroup.plan` / `execute` / `plan_and_execute` accept a `CommandRoutine` wherever they take an action list:

```python
trajectory = await mg.plan(routine)
await mg.execute(trajectory, routine.tcp, routine)
await mg.plan_and_execute(resolve_routine(routine, dataset))  # Dataset routine
```

- **Runs:** line, cartesian PTP, joint PTP and circle motions, and `set_io`. `set_io` works without a trigger or with a time, distance or path-fraction trigger. Boolean, integer and analog values and the controller or bus IO origin are supported.
- **Uses the routine's own context:** TCP, start joint position, motion group setup and default motion settings. Per-command settings win.
- **Dataset poses:** `resolve_routine(routine, dataset)` resolves local pose references and frame poses to world poses first.
- **Rejected before the robot moves:** `wait_for_time`, `wait_for_io`, `pause_on_io`, `marker`, `generated_motion`. These raise `UnsupportedRoutineCommand` naming the command. An unresolvable pose raises `PoseResolutionError` naming the pose.
- **Stop:** cancel the task awaiting the call.
- **How it works:** the routine is translated internally into the existing action list (`nova/cell/routine_execution.py`) and run through the existing plan/execute path. The pinned API client has no routine-execute endpoint, so this gives parity with action lists. Existing plan/execute and action APIs are unchanged.

Also added:
- `docs/command_routines.md`, with the list of unsupported commands.
- `examples/command_routine.py`, using `examples/example_dataset.json` from the dataset example.
- Two specs, one per public seam: `.specs/command-routine/execution/spec.md` (running a routine on a `MotionGroup`) and `.specs/command-routine/pose-resolution/spec.md` (`resolve_routine`).

## How to review

Start with `nova/cell/routine_execution.py` (translation and `resolve_routine`), then the routine handling in `nova/cell/robot_cell.py`, then `docs/command_routines.md`.

## How to test quickly

```bash
# Fast, no robot needed (17 tests)
uv run pytest tests/cell/test_execute_routine.py -v

# Virtual controller, needs .env (NOVA_API, NOVA_ACCESS_TOKEN, CELL_NAME) (5 tests, 6 cases)
uv run pytest tests/nova/cell/motion_group/test_execute_routine.py -v

# The example, on a virtual KUKA. A pass ends with "OUT#1 = False"
cd examples && PYTHONPATH=.. uv run python command_routine.py
```

The unit tests use a gateway double and check what the SDK asks the API to plan and execute, plus the errors the user sees. The integration tests run on a virtual controller and cover:
- a code-built motion routine
- dataset pose resolution
- `set_io` during a run
- an unsupported command being rejected
- the example dataset routine

## Limitations

- **Not yet verified on a real controller.** The run on a real controller is pending, and the ADR 001 hardware check for the IO overlay is still open.
- **Not supported yet:** the five commands above, inline targets with a different TCP, and generated paths.
- **No dedicated execution-state or marker events.** The caller reads `mg.stream_state()` alongside the run.
- **Integration coverage is thin in places.** Integer and analog outputs, time and distance triggers, circle motions and per-command settings are only covered by the gateway-double tests.
- **A failed integration run can leave its controller busy**, which fails the next run until the controller is deleted.

# Spec: Resolve a CommandRoutine against a Dataset

**Parent:** NDX-883
**Seam:** `nova.cell.routine_execution.resolve_routine(routine, dataset)`, which returns a copy of the routine with inline world poses
**Status:** implemented on the virtual controller
**Codebase:** wandelbots-nova
**Related spec:** [Execute CommandRoutines on a MotionGroup](../execution/spec.md), which runs the resolved routine

## Problem Statement

CommandRoutines in a Dataset point at poses taught in that Dataset (local pose references) or at poses given in a Dataset frame. A MotionGroup can only plan world poses, and a routine that still refers to the Dataset cannot run without it. Robot Programmers need taught poses to drive the robot without converting them by hand.

## Solution

`resolve_routine(routine, dataset)` returns a copy of the routine in which every local pose reference and every inline pose given in a Dataset frame is an inline pose in the world frame, keeping its kinematic configuration. The result runs without the Dataset. A pose that cannot be resolved fails with an error naming it, before anything is planned.

## Glossary

- **Local Pose Reference:** a motion target that refers to a pose taught in the owning Dataset by pose id.
- **Dataset:** a NOVA data container holding taught poses, frames and CommandRoutines keyed by routine id.

## Requirements

### R1 Resolve taught poses to world poses

**User Story:** As a Robot Programmer, I want a routine loaded from a Dataset resolved to world poses, so that taught poses drive the robot.

- **R1.1** WHEN a routine contains a Local Pose Reference, `resolve_routine` SHALL replace it by the taught pose in the world frame, including the frames it is taught in, keeping its kinematic configuration.
- **R1.2** WHEN a routine contains an inline pose given in a Dataset frame, `resolve_routine` SHALL replace it by the pose in the world frame.
- **R1.3** `resolve_routine` SHALL resolve motion targets and the via pose of circular motions, and leave joint position targets and all other commands unchanged.
- **R1.4** THE resolved routine SHALL run through the MotionGroup without the Dataset, in the same way as a routine built in code.

### R2 Fail clearly on poses that cannot be resolved

- **R2.1** IF a Local Pose Reference or a frame cannot be resolved against the Dataset, THEN `resolve_routine` SHALL raise `PoseResolutionError` naming the pose or frame, before anything is planned.

## Examples

| ID | Given | When | Then | Test |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| E1 | A local pose `slot` taught 100 mm along x of a frame at x = 1000 mm | the routine is resolved and planned | the planned target is (1100, 0, 0) with the taught kinematic configuration | `TestPoseResolution` (unit) |
| E2 | An inline pose 5 mm along x in that frame | the routine is resolved and planned | the planned target is (1005, 0, 0) | `TestPoseResolution` |
| E3 | A pose on a rotated, nested frame | the routine is resolved | the world pose matches the frame chain | `TestPoseResolution` |
| E4 | A routine pointing at `missing-pose` | the routine is resolved | `PoseResolutionError` names `missing-pose`, nothing is planned | `TestPoseResolution` |
| E5 | A pose taught 50 mm along x of a frame placed at the start TCP pose | the resolved routine runs on a virtual controller | the robot ends 50 mm along x of the start | `TestDatasetPoses` (integration) |

## Implementation Decisions

- **Resolution is separate from execution.** The MotionGroup takes no Dataset; callers resolve first (`plan_and_execute(resolve_routine(routine, dataset))`). This keeps one way to run a routine and lets other code, such as the Dataset service's resolve endpoint (NDX-937), produce routines that run without the Dataset.
- **Existing Dataset resolution.** Poses and frames are resolved through the Dataset's existing frame/pose resolution (`as_world()`); `DatasetError` is wrapped as `PoseResolutionError`.

## Testing Decisions

- **One seam.** Tests call `resolve_routine` and observe the result where it becomes visible, as the targets the planner is asked for, or as the error. No test asserts frame maths owned by the Dataset model beyond these examples.

- [02 Run routines loaded from a Dataset](issues/02-run-routines-from-dataset.md)

## Out of Scope

- Cross-Dataset pose references (`dataset_pose`).

class CommandRoutineRunState(str, Enum):
    """
    The lifecycle state of a command routine run. The states match the states of a program run.  - `PREPARING`: the run was accepted and is getting ready to execute its first command. - `RUNNING`: the routine is executing, see `current_command`. This includes waiting on a `wait_for_io`,   `wait_for_time` or `pause_on_io` command. - `COMPLETED`: the routine executed to the end. - `FAILED`: the run ended with an error, see `error`. - `STOPPED`: the run was stopped by the caller or by an expired timeout.  `COMPLETED`, `FAILED` and `STOPPED` are final.
    """

    """
    allowed enum values
    """
    PREPARING = "PREPARING"
    RUNNING = "RUNNING"
    COMPLETED = "COMPLETED"
    FAILED = "FAILED"
    STOPPED = "STOPPED"

    @classmethod
    def from_json(cls, json_str: str) -> Self:
        """Create an instance of CommandRoutineRunState from a JSON string"""

# Running CommandRoutines

A `CommandRoutine` is an ordered list of commands with its own context (motion group, TCP, start
joint position, default motion settings, motion group setup). You can build one in code
(`nova.command_routines`) or load it from a Dataset. `MotionGroup` runs it the same way it runs
action lists:

| Call | Returns |
| --- | --- |
| `await mg.plan(routine)` | `JointTrajectory` |
| `await mg.execute(joint_trajectory, routine.tcp, routine)` | runs a planned trajectory |
| `await mg.plan_and_execute(routine)` | plans, then runs |

The routine's own context is used and cannot be overridden. Per-command motion settings take
precedence over the routine defaults. Planning only needs the start joint position, so move the
robot there first .

## From code

```python
from nova.command_routines import command_routine, move_joint_ptp, move_linear, set_io

routine = command_routine(
    "my-routine",
    motion_group=mg.id,
    tcp="Flange",
    motion_group_setup=await mg.get_setup("Flange"),
    start_joint_position=list(await mg.joints()),
    commands=[move_joint_ptp(target_joints), set_io("tool_out[0]", True), move_linear(pose_ref)],
)
await mg.plan_and_execute(routine)
```

## From a Dataset

Load the Dataset (for example with `ds.local_dataset(...)` in `@nova.program` preconditions) and
resolve the routine against it. Local pose references and poses in a Dataset frame become inline
world poses, so the calls above need no dataset:

```python
from nova.cell.routine_execution import resolve_routine

routine = ctx.dataset.command_routines["my-routine"]
await mg.plan_and_execute(resolve_routine(routine, ctx.dataset))
```

If the routine's TCP or motion group setup do not match your controller, replace them with
`routine.model_copy(update={"tcp": ..., "motion_group_setup": await mg.get_setup(tcp)})`.
The full flow, with the dataset of `examples/datasets.py`, is in
[`examples/command_routine.py`](../examples/command_routine.py). The command support list is
this page's "Supported commands" and "Not supported yet" sections.

## Supported commands

- Motions: `move_linear`, `move_cartesian_ptp`, `move_joint_ptp` (joint position target),
  `move_circular`.
- `set_io`: boolean, integer and analog outputs, controller or bus IO origin. Without `at` it
  switches at its motion boundary. With a time, distance or path-fraction trigger
  (`at_time`, `at_distance`, `at_path_fraction`) it switches at that point along the motion.

## Not supported yet

`wait_for_time`, `wait_for_io`, `pause_on_io`, `marker` and `generated_motion` have no
action-list equivalent. A routine containing one raises `UnsupportedRoutineCommand` naming the
command (for example `Command 3 (wait_for_time) is not supported yet`) during planning, before
the robot moves. Nothing is skipped silently.

## Observing state, stopping, errors

- **Observe:** run the routine as a task and read `mg.stream_state()` next to it. `state_stream_rate_msecs` sets the
  rate of the state stream used during execution.
- **Stop:** cancel the task awaiting the call. No outputs are written after a stop. Without a
  stop the routine runs to completion.
- **Errors**, all raised before the robot moves:
  - `UnsupportedRoutineCommand`: unsupported command or path type.
  - `PoseResolutionError`: a referenced pose cannot be resolved (error names the pose). Pass the
    Dataset when the routine uses local pose references.
  - `ValueError`: the routine references a different motion group.
  - Planning failures surface as the usual planning errors.
"""
Run a CommandRoutine on a virtual KUKA KR16, reusing the dataset of `datasets.py`.

The dataset's `startup-routine` only holds a `wait_for_time` command, which is not supported yet.
This example therefore drops unsupported commands from the dataset routine and appends explicit
motions to the dataset poses `pick` and `place`, plus two `set_io` commands: one at a motion
boundary and one with a path-fraction trigger. It then plans and runs the routine.

Which commands are supported: see `docs/command_routines.md` ("Supported commands" and
"Not supported yet") and `nova/cell/routine_execution.py`.
"""

import nova
from nova import api, run_program
from nova import datasets as ds
from nova.actions import joint_ptp
from nova.cell import virtual_controller
from nova.cell.routine_execution import resolve_routine
from nova.command_routines import (
    at_path_fraction,
    move_cartesian_ptp,
    move_linear,
    set_io,
    with_settings,
)

# Output that exists on the virtual KUKA controller.
OUTPUT = "OUT#1"

# TODO: Remove this filter once the SDK can execute these commands. Until then a routine
# containing one of them is rejected with `UnsupportedRoutineCommand` before the robot moves.
UNSUPPORTED = ("wait_for_time", "wait_for_io", "pause_on_io", "marker", "generated_motion")


@nova.program(
    id="command_routine",
    name="Command routine",
    preconditions=nova.ProgramPreconditions(
        controllers=[
            virtual_controller(
                name="kuka-kr16-r2010",
                manufacturer=api.models.Manufacturer.KUKA,
                type="kuka-kr16_r2010_2",
            )
        ],
        dataset=ds.local_dataset("example_dataset.json"),
        cleanup_controllers=False,
    ),
)
async def start(ctx: nova.ProgramContext):
    """Run a Dataset routine with explicit motions and set_io, with and without trigger."""
    controller = await ctx.cell.controller("kuka-kr16-r2010")
    motion_group = controller[0]
    tcp = (await motion_group.tcp_names())[0]
    home = tuple(await motion_group.joints())

    slow = api.models.MotionSettings(
        limits_override=api.models.LimitsOverride(tcp_velocity_limit=50)
    )

    fast = api.models.MotionSettings(
        limits_override=api.models.LimitsOverride(tcp_velocity_limit=250)
    )

    dataset_routine = ctx.dataset.command_routines["startup-routine"]
    supported = [c for c in dataset_routine.commands if c.type not in UNSUPPORTED]

    routine = dataset_routine.model_copy(
        update={
            "commands": [
                *supported,
                move_cartesian_ptp("pick"),  # dataset poses are resolved through the dataset
                set_io(OUTPUT, True),  # without trigger: at the motion boundary
                *with_settings(slow, [move_linear("place")]),
                set_io(OUTPUT, False, at=at_path_fraction(0.5)),  # with trigger
                *with_settings(fast, [move_cartesian_ptp("pick")]),
            ],
            # The seed routine carries no context, so take it from the motion group.
            "tcp": tcp,
            "motion_group_setup": await motion_group.get_setup(tcp),
            "start_joint_position": list(home),
        }
    )

    print("Running routine...")
    await motion_group.plan_and_execute(resolve_routine(routine, ctx.dataset))
    await motion_group.plan_and_execute([joint_ptp(home)], tcp)
    print(f"{OUTPUT} = {await controller.read(OUTPUT)}")


if __name__ == "__main__":
    run_program(start)

"""
This example runs the `inspect-30deg` routine of abb-irb-1300-demo.json on a virtual ABB IRB 1300,
once as an action list and once as the dataset's CommandRoutine, to compare both.

This demonstrates:
- Setting up a virtual robot controller
- Connecting to the robot
- Planning and executing basic movements
- Using joint and point-to-point motion types

Key robotics concepts:
- Motion groups: Controllable robot parts (usually the arm)
- TCP (Tool Center Point): The point you control on the robot
- Joint movement (jnt): Move by specifying joint angles in radians
- Point-to-point movement (ptp): Move to a specific position/orientation (x,y,z, rotation angle in radians)
- Pose: Position (x,y,z) and orientation (rx,ry,rz) in 3D space
"""

import asyncio

from nova.cell.routine_execution import resolve_routine
from pydantic import Field

import nova
from nova import api, run_program
from nova import datasets as ds
from nova.actions import cartesian_ptp, circular, joint_ptp, linear
from nova.cell import virtual_controller
from nova.types import MotionSettings, Pose


# Configure the robot program
@nova.program(
    id="start_here",  # Unique identifier of the program. If not provided, the function name will be used.
    name="Start Here",  # Readable name of the program
    # viewer=nova.viewers.Rerun(),  # add this line for a 3D visualization
    preconditions=nova.ProgramPreconditions(
        controllers=[
            virtual_controller(
                name="abb-irb-1300", manufacturer=api.models.Manufacturer.ABB, type="abb-1300_14_7"
            )
        ],
        cleanup_controllers=False,
        dataset=ds.local_dataset("abb-irb-1300-demo.json"),
    ),
)
async def start(
    ctx: nova.ProgramContext,
    count: int = Field(
        default=1, ge=1, le=10, description="The number of times to repeat the movement"
    ),
):
    """Run the dataset routine `inspect-30deg` once as an action list and once as the dataset's CommandRoutine."""
    cell = ctx.cell
    controller = await cell.controller("abb-irb-1300")
    cycle = ctx.cycle(extra={"app": "visual-studio-code"})

    motion_group = controller[0]
    dataset_routine = ctx.dataset.command_routines["inspect-30deg"]
    # The dataset names the TCP "flange"; the virtual controller calls it differently.
    tcp = (await motion_group.tcp_names())[0]
    home = tuple(dataset_routine.start_joint_position)

    # A motion target is a world pose, so resolve the taught poses with `as_world()`.
    def world(pose_id: str) -> Pose:
        return ctx.dataset.poses[pose_id].as_world()

    normal = MotionSettings(tcp_velocity_limit=100)
    fast = MotionSettings(tcp_velocity_limit=200)

    # 1) The routine as an action list.
    actions = [
        joint_ptp(home, settings=normal),
        cartesian_ptp(world("Base-30deg-0m-Via-1"), settings=normal),
        linear(world("Base-30deg-0m-slot-1"), settings=normal),
        cartesian_ptp(world("Base-30deg-0m-appr-1"), settings=normal),
        circular(
            world("Base-30deg-0m-appr-2"),
            intermediate=world("Base-30deg-0m-arc-via"),
            settings=fast,
        ),
        joint_ptp(home, settings=normal),
    ]

    # 2) The routine as stored in the dataset. Its local pose references are resolved to world
    # poses through the dataset. The dataset's TCP name and partial motion group setup do not
    # match this virtual controller, so take both from the motion group.
    routine = dataset_routine.model_copy(
        update={"tcp": tcp, "motion_group_setup": await motion_group.get_setup(tcp)}
    )

    await cycle.start()

    # Both runs start from the routine's start joint position, so move there first.
    await motion_group.plan_and_execute([joint_ptp(home, settings=normal)], tcp)

    for i in range(count):
        # print(f"Run {i + 1} of {count}: action list")
        # joint_trajectory = await motion_group.plan(actions, tcp, start_joint_position=home)
        # await motion_group.execute(joint_trajectory, tcp, actions=actions)
        # await asyncio.sleep(1)

        print(f"Run {i + 1} of {count}: command routine")
        await motion_group.plan_and_execute(resolve_routine(routine, ctx.dataset))
        await asyncio.sleep(1)

    await cycle.finish()

        controller_name = "ur-routine-dataset-test"
        async with Nova() as nova:

                )
            )
            controller = await cell.controller(controller_name)
            async with controller[0] as mg:
                # GIVEN
                start = await mg.joints()
                start_pose = await mg.tcp_pose("Flange")

                now = datetime(2026, 1, 1, tzinfo=timezone.utc)
                dataset = Dataset(
                    dataset="d",
                    revision=1,
                    created_at=now,
                    updated_at=now,
                    frames={"start": DatasetFrame(frame="start", dataset="d", pose=start_pose)},
                    poses={

                )

        async with Nova() as nova:

            await cell.ensure_controller(

                    type="universalrobots-ur10e",
                )
            )
            controller = await cell.controller(controller_name)
            async with controller[0] as mg:
                # GIVEN
                await controller.write("tool_out[0]", False)
                start = list(await mg.joints())
                moved = [start[0] + 0.3, *start[1:]]
                routine = command_routine(
                    "io",
                    motion_group=mg.id,
                    tcp="Flange",
                    motion_group_setup=await mg.get_setup("Flange"),

                    commands=[

                        set_io("tool_out[0]", True),
                        move_joint_ptp(start),
                    ],
                )

                # WHEN
                observed: list[bool] = []

                async def watch():
                    while True:
                        observed.append(bool(await controller.read("tool_out[0]")))
                        await asyncio.sleep(0.05)

                watcher = asyncio.create_task(watch())
                try:
                    await mg.plan_and_execute(routine)
                finally:

                # THEN
                assert observed[0] is False

    @pytest.mark.asyncio
    @pytest.mark.integration
    @pytest.mark.parametrize(
        "command, command_type", [(wait_for_time(500), "wait_for_time"), (marker("here"), "marker")]
    )
    async def test_unsupported_command_is_rejected_before_motion_on_virtual_controller(
        self, command, command_type
    ):
        controller_name = "ur-routine-unsupported-test"
        async with Nova() as nova:
            cell = nova.cell()
            await cell.ensure_controller(
                virtual_controller(
                    name=controller_name,
                    manufacturer=api.models.Manufacturer.UNIVERSALROBOTS,
                    type="universalrobots-ur10e",
                )
            )
            controller = await cell.controller(controller_name)
            async with controller[0] as mg:
                # GIVEN
                start = list(await mg.joints())
                moved = [start[0] + 0.3, *start[1:]]
                routine = command_routine(
                    "unsupported",
                    motion_group=mg.id,
                    tcp="Flange",
                    motion_group_setup=await mg.get_setup("Flange"),
                    start_joint_position=start,
                    commands=[move_joint_ptp(moved), command],
                )

                # WHEN
                with pytest.raises(UnsupportedRoutineCommand) as error:

                # THEN

                assert "not supported yet" in str(error.value)

import asyncio, json, sys, time
from nova import Nova, api
from nova.cell.controllers import virtual_controller
from nova.command_routines import command_routine, move_joint_ptp, set_io, wait_for_time, marker

async def run(api_, r, deadline=20):
    t0 = time.monotonic()
    try:
        run = await api_.start_command_routine_run(cell="cell", command_routine=r)
    except api.ApiException as e:
        print("  start ->", e.status, e.body); return
    print("  started", run.state, run.current_command)
    last = None
    while True:
        run = await api_.get_command_routine_run(cell="cell", run=run.run)
        cur = (run.state, run.current_command, run.error)
        if cur != last: print(f"  {time.monotonic()-t0:5.2f}s", *cur, flush=True); last = cur
        if run.state.value in ("COMPLETED", "FAILED", "STOPPED"): return
        if time.monotonic() - t0 > deadline:
            print("  DEADLINE, stopping", await api_.stop_command_routine_run(cell="cell", run=run.run)); return
        await asyncio.sleep(0.1)

async def main():
    async with Nova() as nova:
        cell = nova.cell()
        await cell.ensure_controller(virtual_controller(name="ur-routine-probe",
            manufacturer=api.models.Manufacturer.UNIVERSALROBOTS, type="universalrobots-ur10e"))
        controller = await cell.controller("ur-routine-probe")
        api_ = api.api.CommandRoutineExecutionApi(api_client=nova.api._api_client)
        async with controller[0] as mg:
            setup = await mg.get_setup("Flange")
            def routine(*cmds, **kw):
                return command_routine("probe", **({"motion_group": mg.id, "tcp": "Flange", "motion_group_setup": setup} | kw), commands=list(cmds))
            for case in sys.argv[1:]:
                start = list(await mg.joints()); moved = [start[0] + 0.3, *start[1:]]
                print("==", case, "start", [round(j, 2) for j in start], flush=True)
                if case == "plan":
                    raw = await api_.plan_command_routine_without_preload_content(cell="cell", command_routine=routine(move_joint_ptp(moved), start_joint_position=start))
                    d = json.loads(await raw.read()); print("  ", raw.status, list(d), d.get("joint_trajectory", {}).get("locations", [None])[-1])
                elif case == "plan-nomg":
                    raw = await api_.plan_command_routine_without_preload_content(cell="cell", command_routine=routine(move_joint_ptp(moved), start_joint_position=start, motion_group=None))
                    print("  ", raw.status, (await raw.read())[:300])
                elif case == "plan-nostart":
                    raw = await api_.plan_command_routine_without_preload_content(cell="cell", command_routine=routine(move_joint_ptp(moved)))
                    print("  ", raw.status, (await raw.read())[:300])
                elif case == "plan-marker":
                    raw = await api_.plan_command_routine_without_preload_content(cell="cell", command_routine=routine(move_joint_ptp(moved), marker("m"), start_joint_position=start))
                    print("  ", raw.status, (await raw.read())[:200])
                elif case == "motion":
                    await run(api_, routine(move_joint_ptp(moved), move_joint_ptp(start), start_joint_position=start))
                elif case == "one":
                    await run(api_, routine(move_joint_ptp(moved), start_joint_position=start))
                elif case == "io":
                    await run(api_, routine(move_joint_ptp(moved), set_io("tool_out[0]", True), move_joint_ptp(start), start_joint_position=start))
                    print("  io", await controller.read("tool_out[0]")); await controller.write("tool_out[0]", False)
                elif case == "wait":
                    await run(api_, routine(move_joint_ptp(moved), wait_for_time(500), marker("m"), move_joint_ptp(start), start_joint_position=start))
                elif case == "notatstart":
                    await run(api_, routine(move_joint_ptp(start), start_joint_position=moved))
                elif case == "nostart":
                    await run(api_, routine(move_joint_ptp(moved)))
asyncio.run(main())
EOF

"""Ergonomic constructors for the NOVA CommandRoutine command types.

These factories wrap the generated ``api.models.*`` command routine models so a
``CommandRoutineBuilder`` (and its callers) can assemble a routine without importing
the generated classes directly.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

from typing import Any

from nova import api

# --- I/O values ------------------------------------------------------------


def io_value(io: str, value: bool | int | float) -> api.models.IOValue:
    """Build the discriminated ``IOValue`` for a digital, integer or analog output.

    ``bool`` maps to a boolean value, ``int`` to an integer value (transmitted as a
    string to avoid precision loss) and ``float`` to an analog value.
    """
    # bool is a subclass of int, so it must be checked first.
    if isinstance(value, bool):
        return api.models.IOBooleanValue(io=io, value=value)
    if isinstance(value, int):
        return api.models.IOIntegerValue(io=io, value=str(value))
    if isinstance(value, float):
        return api.models.IOFloatValue(io=io, value=value)
    raise TypeError(f"Unsupported I/O value type: {type(value)!r}")


# --- Pose references -------------------------------------------------------


def local_pose(pose_id: str) -> api.models.LocalPoseReference:
    """Reference a pose taught in the enclosing dataset."""
    return api.models.LocalPoseReference(dataset_pose=pose_id)


def joint_position(joints: list[float]) -> api.models.JointPositionReference:
    """Target a joint configuration (radians)."""
    return api.models.JointPositionReference(joints=joints)


def _as_pose_ref(target: api.models.PoseRef | str) -> api.models.PoseRef:
    """Coerce a bare pose id into a :func:`local_pose` reference."""
    return local_pose(target) if isinstance(target, str) else target


def _as_joint_ref(target: api.models.PoseRef | list[float]) -> api.models.PoseRef:
    """Coerce a bare joint list into a :func:`joint_position` reference."""
    return joint_position(target) if isinstance(target, list) else target
